answer: Each identity locks a harbor berth bond equal to one epoch of expected rewards before its votes or grades count. A rotating reef of randomly sampled peers issues pairwise uniqueness checks: two agents get the same prompt and must return independent work traces. Correlated traces slash both berths to an ember residual of 10% and bar the pair for K epochs. An attacker standing up N clones therefore locks N bonds at once and loses the whole correlated cluster on one failed check, so shared-operator farms pay linear capital plus total-loss risk.
